messages:
Maya: Quick perf note — after the kernel-selector change landed yesterday, Llama-2 70B inference on our hosted pool shows a tail latency bump at ~2k context. Anyone else seeing this?
Kevin: Yep, saw a tiny spike in p99 for the ml-infer group. Preliminary profiling points to a kernel fallback for attention around seq>1024.
Rigel: My run confirmed that. The selector picks generic_attn instead of fmha_path when head_dim != expected, so we pay memcpy + extra kernels.
Tess: Pasting a brief profile snippet from a failing trace: ```text
PROFILE: model=llama-2-70b
seq=2048 batch=1
kernel_selected=generic_attn (fallback)
kv_cache_memcpy=120ms
attention_kernel=generic_attn (220ms)
total_token_ms=15.2
```
Maya: Thanks — that kv memcpy number is suspicious. Could be KV layout mismatch when head_dim/num_heads quantization changes head stride.
Kevin: Also noticed rope_theta defaults differ between our L2 loader and the model registry. If rope_theta scaling mismatch happens, the runtime switches code path for rotary embedding, triggering slower operator.
Rigel: Suggested quick fixes: 1) unify rope_theta defaults in model metadata, 2) relax kernel selector to accept head_dim multiples with a small tolerance, 3) add a fast memcpy-path for kv cache when stride differs.
Tess: Quick config we tested locally: ```json
{
  "rope_theta": 10000,
  "head_dim": 128,
  "num_heads": 64,
  "norm_type": "rmsnorm",
  "activation": "silu",
  "kernel_policy": "prefer_fmha"
}
```
Tess: With that the selector stayed on fmha_path and p99 dropped ~18%.
Maya: Nice. Two follow-ups: (A) can eng-runtime add a guard so kernel_selector logs when it falls back + reason, (B) infra to run a micro-benchmark across model variants (Llama2-13B/70B, Llama3-12B) for head_dim/head_count combos.
Kevin: I can add the selector logs today — will include head_dim, num_heads, rope_theta, and chosen kernel. Helpful to triage in SLO dashboards.
Rigel: I'll prototype the fast kv memcpy (CUDA kernel) — should remove the 120ms memcpy for 2k contexts. Rough ETA EOD tomorrow.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: perf-logs enabled on canary cluster, sampling=1%.
Maya: Great. Also flagging model onboarding docs: ensure loader normalizes rmsnorm vs layernorm and documents SiLU vs GELU assumptions — some of our model forks changed activations and that affects kernel choices.
Tess: One more data point: mixtral variants with odd head dims triggered the same fallback but at smaller seq lengths. So the selector tolerance needs to consider both head_dim and sequence distribution.
Maya: Agreed. Action items: Kevin -> selector logs, Rigel -> kv memcpy kernel, Tess -> run the micro-bench matrix and post results, Maya -> update model metadata guidelines. We'll reconvene in #eng-runtime tomorrow. :thumbsup:
